attachments.document_title: Employment contract or other record of its terms
attachments.label: A1
attachments.text:
FIXED-TERM EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT (excerpt)

Clause 1 - Position
Project assistant, renovation projects, Kriens portfolio. Full-time.

Clause 2 - Duration
The employment begins on 18 June 2025. It is concluded for a fixed term and ends without notice on 17 June 2027.

Clause 3 - Salary
CHF 2,390 gross per month, paid twelve times a year.

Clause 7 - Early termination
Before the end of the fixed term, either party may terminate this contract early with a notice period of three months to the end of a calendar month. This applies from the first day of employment.

Clause 9 - Form
Amendments to this contract must be made in writing.

Kriens, 2 June 2025

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the employer give as the cause of the dismissal the employee's absence from work, and does the employee say they were prevented from working through no fault of their own (for instance illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Did the employer end the employment relationship with immediate effect, without a notice period?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the immediate dismissal in writing?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Has the employee earned income from other work during the time the notice period or the agreed term would still have run?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Was the employment relationship agreed for a fixed term, with an agreed end date, rather than for an unlimited period?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

text:
Dear team,

When I signed with Seematt Property Ltd I made a point of reading the clause about leaving, because I'd been burned before. My written contract says that either side can end it early, but only with three months' notice to the end of a month. That's longer than the usual one month you get in the first year, and that was the whole reason I felt safe taking the job.

The job itself was never meant to be open-ended. It was a fixed contract: I started on 18 June 2025 and it runs until 17 June 2027, when it simply ends on that date. That was agreed from the start because they needed someone for the renovation of their buildings in Kriens.

I'm attaching the contract so you can see the start date, the end date and the notice clause for yourself.

Now the problem. On 18 January 2026 Anna Palmer, who manages the Kriens office, phoned me in the evening and told me I was out, effective immediately. Not in three months, not at the end of the month: that same day. She said I shouldn't come in the next morning and that my access badge had already been switched off. Paul Frei from maintenance told me the next day that my desk had been cleared.

My salary was CHF 2,390 a month. I don't understand how a contract with a fixed end date and a three-month notice clause can just be torn up over the phone. What can I do to get what I'm owed?

Thanks in advance,
Megan Morgan
Mattenweg 137, Kriens
